meta.subtitle: A pure-play automation company priced near its 52-week low, with guidance raised and the spin-off arithmetic still confusing the data

analystCommentary:
Honeywell became a different company one day before the quarter closed. On June 29, 2026 it spun off Honeywell Aerospace, executed a one-for-two reverse stock split and began reporting as Honeywell Technologies, a pure-play automation company with three segments: Building Automation, Process Automation and Technology, and Industrial Automation. The second-quarter 10-Q still consolidates Aerospace, so almost every trailing figure on this page describes the old company; the financials section explains the translation once, and we work from the release's Honeywell Technologies tables and the 2026 guidance throughout.

On that basis the quarter was good. Honeywell Technologies sales were $5,187 million, up 4% organically, segment margin expanded 100 basis points to 19.0%, adjusted EPS rose 10% to $1.95, and orders grew 16% to a $20 billion backlog. Guidance was raised on organic growth, segment margin and adjusted EPS; the sales range was trimmed only for the early closing of two divestitures, and cash-flow guidance was unchanged. The Street's consensus target of $261.82 sits +30.0% above the price, with 20 Buys and no Sells.

We rate the shares BUY with a target range of $215–$255, below consensus for the three reasons the thesis sets out. The shares trade near the bottom of their 52-week range at ~20.2x FY27E EPS of $9.99, and nothing captured since July 2, 2026 explains the move; the headline window closed before it, and that silence leads the risk section. The case rests on what is disclosed: a raised outlook, an order book growing faster than sales, and a three-year plan management put at approximately $12 of adjusted EPS.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Honeywell International Inc., which now describes itself as Honeywell Technologies, is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, and after the June 29, 2026 spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace it is a pure-play automation company serving the building, industrial and process sectors with more than 50,000 employees per the release. It manages three reportable segments: Building Automation; Process Automation and Technology, formed in Q1 2026 from UOP and the core of the former Process Solutions business; and Industrial Automation, which holds sensing and safety technologies, smart energy, thermal solutions and process measurement, and which is selling its Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions businesses in two transactions expected to close in the third quarter of 2026. On July 17, 2026 it acquired Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies business for $1,750 million net of cash, to sit inside Process Automation and Technology, and it retains a 48% equity-method stake in Quantinuum, which completed its IPO on June 4, 2026.

The vendor's segment chart cannot show this company. Its FY25 mix uses four legacy labels, Aerospace at 46.8% ($17.5B), Safety And Productivity Solutions at 25.1% ($9.4B), Home And Building Technologies at 19.7% ($7.4B) and Energy and Sustainability Solutions at 8.4% ($3.1B). Aerospace has since been distributed to shareholders; within Energy and Sustainability Solutions, Advanced Materials left as Solstice Advanced Materials on October 30, 2025 and UOP moved into Process Automation and Technology; the moat section maps each label to what remains. The geographic split, United States 58.2%, Europe 21.7% and Other International 20.2%, is likewise the pre-spin FY25 company, and it measures a different quantity from the 10-Q's statement that international operations, including U.S. exports, represent more than half of sales.

The shape of the remaining company is visible in the release's second-quarter tables: Building Automation leads the three by sales at $2,002 million and by segment margin at 27.1%, Process Automation and Technology is the cyclical one at $1,679 million with orders running ahead of sales, and Industrial Automation at $1,501 million is the one being reshaped by divestiture.

thesis.body:
The thesis is that the market is pricing the new Honeywell Technologies off the old Honeywell's data. Every trailing multiple on this page, the 7.8x P/E, the 7.1x EV/EBITDA, the FY25 revenue of $37.4B, belongs to a conglomerate that no longer exists, and the quarter's reported EPS of $17.83 carries a $15.78 after-tax gain on the deconsolidation of Quantinuum. What is left is a company whose segment margin is guided to exit 2026 above 22% and to reach 24% over three years, growing orders far faster than sales, and guiding adjusted EPS of $8.05 to $8.35 for 2026 with a three-year earnings path management has put a number on.

On that forward earnings base the 30-analyst consensus, with no Sells, sits well above the price. We rate the shares BUY on the disclosed fundamentals, with a target range below consensus for three reasons: nothing captured after July 2, 2026 explains the decline the risk section describes, no post-spin balance sheet has been filed, and the Process Automation and Technology inflection promised for the second half has to show up in shipped catalyst, not orders. The counter-case is a company whose guided free cash flow is a fraction of the conglomerate's, priced at a forward multiple that peers, still pending on this page, cannot yet test.

catalysts: Process Automation and Technology's guided second-half inflection to high-single-digit growth as catalyst shipments and LNG projects convert a book-to-bill above 1.2; the growth section carries the figures.
Closing of the Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions sales by early August, which simplifies Industrial Automation and is already in guidance.
Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies, closed July 17, 2026, entering the second-half numbers with commercial and cost synergies management says it can see.

The margin bridge: a quick step from stranded-cost removal, portfolio actions and the aerospace trademark agreement, then steady annual expansion toward the three-year target; the moat section carries the figures.
A decision on the Quantinuum stake, which management expects to set out by early next year; the stake is carried at equity and produced a $265 million equity loss in the quarter.
risks: An unexplained move: the shares sit near the bottom of their 52-week range and nothing captured after July 2, 2026 accounts for it; the risk section says what that does and does not tell us.
The spin-off's arithmetic: trailing multiples, the segment chart and the FY25 tables all describe the pre-spin conglomerate; the financials section carries the translation.
Process Automation and Technology's margin fell 180 basis points in the quarter on lower catalyst volumes and mix while its orders rose; the guidance now depends on that reversing.
Tariffs, the Middle East conflict and Russia obligations, all named in the 10-Q's updated risk factors for a company whose international operations exceed half of sales.
Governance: the Chairman and CEO roles are combined and the April 2026 proxy predates the spin-off; the management section carries what the excerpt does and does not show.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The Facts block above needs translating before it can be read, and this is the one place the report does it. The FY21–FY25 income series ($34.4B to $37.4B of revenue, diluted EPS of $15.82 to $14.72) is the conglomerate that included Aerospace and, until late October 2025, Advanced Materials; consensus FY26E revenue of $20.1B is Honeywell Technologies alone, so the -46% the snapshot prints beside it is a change of company, not a forecast. The per-share history has also been restated for the one-for-two reverse stock split. The quarter's figures are consolidated: the 10-Q still includes Aerospace and will present it as discontinued operations from the third quarter, and the snapshot's Q2'26 revenue of $9.7B (-6%) compares the vendor's quarter with an unrecast prior year, while the release compares $9,719 million with a recast $9,322 million and shows growth; the report uses the release. Reported EPS of $17.83 includes a gain on deconsolidation of Quantinuum of $15.78 after tax, less $1.54 after tax of divestiture-related costs, which is why the trailing P/E of 7.8x is not a valuation input.

What matters is the Honeywell Technologies table. Second-quarter sales were $5,187 million, up 3% reported and 4% organically; segment profit rose 9% to $985 million and segment margin expanded 100 basis points to 19.0%, while operating margin slipped 50 basis points to 12.8% because separation costs and corporate expense sit below the segment line. Adjusted EPS was $1.95, up from $1.77, after a $0.16 headwind from a higher adjusted tax rate. By segment, Building Automation earned $542 million at a 27.1% margin, Process Automation and Technology $371 million at 22.1%, down 180 basis points on lower catalyst volumes and unfavorable mix, and Industrial Automation $258 million at 17.2%. At the consolidated level, gross margin fell 170 basis points to 37.6% on higher material and labor costs, company-funded research and development rose to $524 million, and other expense carried approximately $0.7 billion of Aerospace Spin-Off costs.
financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance-sheet table is the pre-spin company at each year end: total debt of $34.6B and net debt of $22.1B at FY25, more than double the FY21 net debt, as acquisitions and the pre-separation debt financing described in the 10-Q were layered on, with total equity of $15.4B and a current ratio of 1.32. None of it says what Honeywell Technologies owes today: the second-quarter balance sheet is not among the captured excerpts, and the spin-off, the debt tender offers and redemptions (a $241 million loss on extinguishment year to date) and the Catalyst Technologies purchase all moved it, at or after the quarter end. The trailing net debt to EBITDA of 2.0x and interest coverage of 3.5x carry the same pre-spin numerator and denominator.

What the 10-Q does establish is the direction: interest and other financial charges rose to $363 million in the quarter from $329 million on debt raised ahead of the separation, net of tenders, and management said on the call that lower net interest expense from debt paydown helped the adjusted EPS bridge. The company also now carries Quantinuum at equity after the June 4, 2026 IPO, a 48% stake in the 10-Q's words and 47% in the transcript's; we use the 10-Q. Until the third-quarter filing shows the standalone balance sheet, leverage is a gap in this report, and we treat it as a risk rather than an assumption.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
The cash-flow table is pre-spin too: operating cash flow of $6.4B and free cash flow of $5.4B in FY25, a 14.4% margin, with $3.8B of repurchases and $3.0B of dividends, describe a company that has since distributed Aerospace to its shareholders. The forward number is the one to hold: Honeywell Technologies guides free cash flow of approximately $2.0B for 2026 on operating cash flow of about $2.1B, at approximately 95% conversion, with the majority in the second half. The second quarter delivered $456 million of free cash flow on the Honeywell Technologies basis, up from $114 million a year earlier per the release, and management put the quarter's capital deployment at $1 billion, roughly $800 million of dividends and roughly $200 million of capital expenditure, with over $2.8 billion deployed year to date across repurchases, dividends and investment.

We chose no highlight cells, because every candidate in the list, from FY25 free cash flow to FY25 net debt, describes the pre-spin conglomerate. The judgment on cash is simple: at that free-cash-flow level the new company converts earnings well but generates far less cash than the old one did, so the dividend and buyback capacity investors remember from the conglomerate has to be re-based, and no standalone dividend has yet been disclosed in the sources we have.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $201.38 the shares trade at 24.2x NTM earnings and ~20.2x FY27E EPS of $9.99, with a 2.21% dividend yield behind which no dividend rate is disclosed on this page. The trailing multiples are not usable: the 7.8x P/E and 7.1x EV/EBITDA rest on earnings that include the Quantinuum gain and on a debt figure from before the spin-off, and P/S of 1.8x divides by conglomerate revenue. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source, so the forward multiple cannot be called rich or cheap against the group; it can be argued against management's own bridge, in which approximately $12 of adjusted EPS in three years implies more than 10% annual growth, and consensus FY26E EPS of $8.32 sits inside the guided range.

The Street is constructive: 30 analysts, Buy 20, Hold 10, Sell 0, with a consensus target of $261.82 (+30.0%), a median of $263.00 and a range of $239.00–$293.00; the two post-spin broker notes captured, from Daiwa and Deutsche Bank, were written on June 30, 2026, before the decline. The current price sits against a 52-week range of $195.87 – $260.28. Our view is that the forward multiple is fair for a business guided to double-digit earnings growth and a segment margin in the low-to-mid twenties, and that the gap to consensus is the market's discount for what it cannot yet see: the post-spin balance sheet, the standalone dividend, and whether the process business inflects.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: The second-half inflection lands: Process Automation and Technology grows high single digits as catalyst shipments and LNG projects convert, organic growth reaches the 4% to 6% guided for the second half, segment margin exits 2026 above 22%, and the market re-rates a pure-play automation company toward the Street's $261.82 consensus target as the post-spin balance sheet and dividend are disclosed.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Guidance is met: adjusted EPS of $8.05 to $8.35 for 2026, consensus FY27E EPS of $9.99 and free cash flow of approximately $2.0B; the shares keep the 24.2x NTM multiple they carry today as the market rolls forward to FY27E earnings, which is approximately $242.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The process inflection slips as Middle East collections and energy-project timing push catalyst volumes into 2027, tariffs and input costs push segment margin back below the quarter's 19.0% rather than toward the guided 20.1% to 20.5%, the standalone balance sheet shows more leverage than the market expected after the Catalyst Technologies purchase, and the multiple compresses below the ~20.2x on FY27E the shares already carry.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight the Base case at 50% and split the remainder evenly between the Bull case at $262 and the Bear case at $170. The probability-weighted value sits above the current price by a low-double-digit percentage, inside the BUY envelope, and the $215–$255 target range brackets the Base case. The Base case is guidance delivered and the market rolling today's next-twelve-month multiple forward one year, with no re-rating assumed. The Bull case needs the process inflection to be visible in shipments by the fourth quarter and the standalone balance sheet to be unremarkable; orders and backlog already point that way, shipped catalyst does not yet. The Bear case is there because the shares have already fallen on information the captured record does not contain, and a report that cannot see the reason should not assume it is benign; the three gaps the thesis names are the three the Bear case widens.

A move to STRONG BUY would need the cause of the decline to be disclosed and dismissed, and the process business to print the inflection. A move to HOLD would follow a cut to the 2026 organic growth or margin guidance, or a standalone balance sheet that forces the dividend or buyback to be rebased below what the market assumes.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.body: Aerospace is in the chart because the vendor's FY25 mix predates the spin-off: on the spin-off date it was distributed to shareholders as Honeywell Aerospace, one share for every two Honeywell shares, and it now trades as HONA. The second-quarter 10-Q still consolidates it, and the release reports the former segment's sales of $4.5 billion, up organically on commercial aviation original equipment up 17% and growth in the aftermarket, with segment profit of $1.1 billion including approximately $40 million of inventory obsolescence charges. From the third quarter it becomes discontinued operations, and Honeywell Technologies holds no shares in it; nothing in this report's valuation depends on it, and the residual link is a trademark agreement management cites as a margin benefit.

segments.name: Home And Building Technologies
segments.body: The vendor's Home And Building Technologies label maps to today's Building Automation segment, the anchor of the remaining company. Second-quarter sales were $2,002 million, up 9% organically with building products and reported sales both up 10%, segment profit was $542 million and segment margin 27.1%, up 90 basis points on volume leverage and pricing, with fire growing in double digits and solutions up 7% on services. Orders rose 13%, led by data center and hospitality per the release; across what management calls its high-growth verticals, which it lists as healthcare, hospitality and data centers, it put orders growth above 50% and organic sales growth at 30%. The installed base and the fire franchise are the moat here; the exposure is construction cycles and channel inventory, which the 10-Q's risk factors name for this segment.

segments.name: Safety And Productivity Solutions
segments.body: The vendor's Safety And Productivity Solutions label is the ancestor of Industrial Automation, which after the Q1 2026 realignment holds sensing and safety technologies, smart energy, thermal solutions and process measurement, plus the Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions businesses that are held for sale, carried a $311 million impairment year to date, and are expected to close by early August. Second-quarter sales were $1,501 million, lower on a reported basis after the personal protective equipment divestiture but up 4% organically, with solutions the growth driver on utilities projects and warehouse backlog; segment margin expanded to 17.2% from 16.3% on pricing and productivity. For the core that remains, orders grew 11% per the call, with sensing and industrial measurement orders up over 20%. This is the segment being fixed rather than the one carrying the moat, and management's own word for the program is a turnaround.

segments.name: Energy and Sustainability Solutions
segments.body: The vendor's Energy and Sustainability Solutions label covered UOP and Advanced Materials; Advanced Materials left as Solstice Advanced Materials in October 2025, and UOP joined the core of Process Solutions in Q1 2026 to form Process Automation and Technology, the segment this label now maps to. Second-quarter sales were $1,679 million, down 1% organically, as projects grew 5% on LNG and a return to growth in automation projects while aftermarket fell 6% on last year's higher catalyst shipments; segment profit was $371 million at a 22.1% margin, down on catalyst volumes and mix. Orders rose 24% on LNG demand and book-to-bill ran above 1.2, and the Johnson Matthey Catalyst Technologies business acquired in July adds to the installed base across refining, petrochemicals and renewable fuels. The second-half inflection has to come from here, and so does the cyclical risk.

moatFactors.name: Installed base and aftermarket
moatFactors.body: The strategy management laid out at Investor Day is to grow the installed base and monetize it through outcome-based services, software and annual recurring revenue on the Honeywell Technologies Forge layer, and the quarter shows the base at work: total-company book-to-bill was 1.1 and Honeywell Technologies' ending backlog rose to $20 billion. The counter is that aftermarket also held the quarter's weakness, with Process Automation and Technology aftermarket sales down on catalyst timing, so the base monetizes on the customer's schedule, not the company's.

moatFactors.name: Domain depth in mission-critical environments
moatFactors.body: Honeywell Technologies describes its markets as ones where uptime, safety, productivity and efficiency are paramount, and the release's segment detail supports the premium in Building Automation, where fire and building products carry a segment margin above the other two segments', and in Process Automation and Technology, where UOP's process technology and catalysts tie customers to licensed processes. The counter is Industrial Automation, where the 10-Q's own risk factor names new entrants, new technologies and product commoditization, and where management is running a turnaround to win back share.

moatFactors.name: Scale after simplification
moatFactors.body: More than 50,000 employees serve the building, industrial and process sectors under the Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system, and management's margin bridge has two parts: over 200 basis points of expansion quickly, from stranded-cost removal, portfolio actions in Industrial Automation and the aerospace trademark agreement, then 60 basis points a year from price, mix, new products and productivity toward the target it set for three years out. The counter is that corporate costs previously spread across Aerospace now sit on a smaller base, which is the gap between segment and operating margin the financials section quantifies, and the bridge assumes it closes quickly.

moatFactors.name: Portfolio in motion
moatFactors.body: Since 2025 the company has spun off Solstice Advanced Materials and Honeywell Aerospace, taken Quantinuum public and kept a large stake, agreed to sell Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions, and bought Catalyst Technologies, while a segment realignment in Q1 2026 recast the reporting lines. Each step is defensible; together they mean that no five-year series on this page describes the company that exists, that the divestitures reduced the 2026 revenue expectation by approximately $400 million, and that the moat has to be judged on one quarter of standalone-style disclosure. That is a weakness of evidence rather than of franchise, and we rate the moat narrow partly for that reason.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is narrow because two of the three segments are cyclical, and the durable economics sit in the third, Building Automation: a fire and building-products franchise with margins above the company's and orders growing faster than sales. Process Automation and Technology's licensed process technology and catalysts are durable in the sense that customers return for reloads, but the quarter showed how lumpy that is, and Industrial Automation is being reshaped. What would widen the moat is the shift to services, software and recurring revenue that management made the center of its strategy; what would narrow it is commoditization in sensing and products, which the 10-Q names, and a capital-allocation history that has been about portfolio surgery rather than reinvestment for three years. Our view is that the franchise deserves the benefit of the doubt on the installed base and not yet on recurring revenue, because no recurring-revenue figure is disclosed in the sources we have.

points: Guidance was raised on July 23, 2026 on the three lines that matter: organic growth to 3% to 4% from 2% to 3%, segment margin to 20.1% to 20.5% with expansion of 250 to 290 basis points, and adjusted EPS to $8.05 to $8.35, up 25% to 29%, with the second half at 4% to 6% organic growth; the sales range of $19.8 billion to $20.0 billion is lower than before only because the divestitures close about two months early, and cash-flow guidance is unchanged.

Orders lead sales: Honeywell Technologies orders grew 16% organically, four times the pace of sales, backlog rose 9%, and every segment posted double-digit short-cycle orders growth per the call; Building Automation orders rose 13% and Process Automation and Technology orders by nearly a quarter, with roughly 50% growth in process technology. The counter is that orders convert on customer schedules, and the process book converts on the longest cycle.

Process Automation and Technology is the swing factor: sales fell 1% organically in the quarter as aftermarket declined on prior-year catalyst shipments, yet the guidance assumes the segment accelerates to high-single-digit growth in the second half; the risk section carries the mechanism and the case against.

Building Automation is compounding: products growing in double digits and solutions up 7% in the quarter, orders up in data center and hospitality, and a mid-single-digit-plus organic outlook for the year; the risk factor is construction activity and channel inventory.

The three-year frame: management targets approximately $12 of adjusted EPS, more than 10% annual growth, on a 24% segment margin target, with the quick margin bridge the moat section describes and cash conversion improving to over 90% with line of sight to 95%; consensus has FY27E EPS at $9.99 on revenue of $20.5B, which is consistent with the path but not yet with the end point.

Consensus FY26E EPS of $8.32 sits inside the guided range, while consensus FY26E revenue of $20.1B sits just above the sales guidance, which was trimmed for divestiture timing the consensus mean may not yet carry; the growth debate is not 2026 but whether the process inflection and the catalyst acquisition make 2027 a double-digit year.

management.leadership: Vimal Kapur is chairman and chief executive officer, as the release styles him, and the April 2026 proxy says he is the one director who is not independent; the same proxy names an independent Lead Director and records the Board's affirmative determination that each of the non-employee nominees it lists, from Mr. Angove to Ms. Nooyi, satisfies the Nasdaq and SEC independence criteria. On execution, the team has delivered a transformation on schedule: the Solstice spin-off in October 2025, the Quantinuum IPO in June 2026, the Aerospace spin-off at the end of that month, the Catalyst Technologies purchase in July and two divestitures closing about two months early, and it raised its growth, margin and earnings outlook in its opening quarter as a standalone company rather than resetting it. Our reservation is that one standalone-style quarter is all the record shows, and nothing captured after early July shows how the market has received it; a management team that has spent three years on portfolio surgery now has to be judged on operating a smaller company, and that judgment cannot yet be made.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is mid-transformation. In the second quarter the company deployed $1 billion, roughly $800 million of dividends and roughly $200 million of capital expenditure per the call, and over $2.8 billion year to date including repurchases; the FY25 table shows $3.8B of repurchases and $3.0B of dividends for the conglomerate, a payout the new company's approximately $2.0B of free cash flow cannot sustain unchanged, and no standalone dividend policy has been disclosed. The two large moves are the $1,750 million purchase of Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies, which adds installed base in refining, petrochemicals and renewable fuels to Process Automation and Technology, and the sale of Productivity Solutions and Services and Warehouse and Workflow Solutions, which took a $311 million impairment year to date and reduces 2026 revenue by approximately $400 million. Debt was raised ahead of the separation and partly tendered back at a $241 million loss year to date. Our judgment: buying catalysts at the bottom of a catalyst cycle is the right timing if the inflection comes, and the divestitures are consistent with the pure-play strategy; the open question is the payout, which management has not re-based in anything we have.
management.governance: The proxy is the April 10, 2026 statement, filed before the Aerospace spin-off, and its excerpt is thin: it carries the independence determinations, the Management Development and Compensation Committee's list of factors, and the treatment of unvested equity in the Solstice spin-off, but no say-on-pay result, no pay tables, no related-person transactions section, no table of holders above 5%, and nothing on how unvested awards were treated in the Aerospace distribution, which came after the proxy's date; we make no claim on any of those. What it does show is a compensation philosophy that reserves judgment: the committee does not target a specific competitive position relative to the market, weighs execution against strategic initiatives, and considered throughout 2025 how to balance pay for performance with retention through the spin-offs. Unvested awards were adjusted with conversion ratios to preserve their pre-spin value when Solstice was distributed, one share for every four Honeywell shares on October 30, 2025. Independence is affirmed for every non-employee nominee, with the Chairman and CEO as the one non-independent director.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy's ownership table as of March 27, 2026, before the one-for-two reverse stock split, shows Mr. Kapur with 46,954 shares beneficially owned, 305,611 shares he had the right to acquire and 1,967 other stock-based holdings, 354,532 in total, and all directors, nominees and executive officers as a group of 22 people at 972,188 shares including 692,593 rights to acquire. Every individual and the group held less than 1% of the shares outstanding. The pattern is the usual one for a large-cap industrial: executive exposure sits in options and units rather than in owned stock, so alignment is to the share price rather than to control, and neither a beneficial-owner table nor insider transaction data is among the captured sources.

idiosyncratic: The move nothing explains. The shares closed at $201.38 on September 14, 2026, near the bottom of a 52-week range of $195.87 – $260.28, and the headline window ends on July 2, 2026. The last broker actions specific to Honeywell are dated June 30: one upgrade, Daiwa to Outperform with a $255 target, and Deutsche Bank maintaining Buy at a raised $263; the July 2 items concern a community-solar project and BMO's initiation on Honeywell Aerospace, a different issuer, and Honeywell Aerospace was due to report standalone results on August 5 with nothing captured on what it said. We treat the decline as unexplained rather than benign.

Process Automation and Technology timing. The segment's margin fell 180 basis points to 22.1% and aftermarket sales fell 6% on last year's catalyst shipments, yet guidance now rests on a second-half inflection to high-single-digit growth as energy projects resume, backlog converts and catalyst volumes rise. The evidence for is the order growth and book-to-bill the moat section gives; the evidence against is the collection headwinds in the Middle East the CFO cited, which sit in this segment's geography, and the 10-Q's risk factor naming oil and gas price volatility and customers' capital availability for refinery construction.

Spin-off costs and the standalone cost base. Other expense carried approximately $0.7 billion of Aerospace Spin-Off costs in the quarter and approximately $0.9 billion year to date, the effective tax rate rose 670 basis points on transaction-related tax costs and foreign tax accruals, and operating margin sat well below segment margin because separation costs and corporate expense sit between them. Management's bridge assumes stranded costs are eliminated quickly; if they linger, the quick step in the margin bridge becomes the gap between guidance and results.

Balance sheet after the separation. The debt figures on this page are pre-spin, interest and other financial charges rose to $363 million on pre-separation financing, the Catalyst Technologies purchase added consideration after the quarter end, and standalone leverage has not been disclosed in anything filed so far. A company with the conglomerate's payout habits, a fraction of its cash flow and a fresh acquisition has less room than its history suggests.

Quantinuum. The equity-method stake produced a $6,629 million gain on deconsolidation and then a $265 million equity loss in the quarter, and management says it will set out plans for the stake by early next year; the stake is an asset whose value no captured source sizes and whose losses now flow through the income statement below the line.
risks.systemic: The systemic exposures are those the 10-Q's updated risk factors put first for the new company: with international operations, including U.S. exports, representing more than half of sales, it faces tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, sanctions and trade barriers, currency swings, the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and its effect on energy markets and shipping, and remaining obligations to Russian counterparties for which the company says it cannot estimate losses beyond current accruals. The MD&A adds elevated inflation and market volatility, moderating global growth and constrained materials, mitigated by dual sourcing, pricing actions and supply-chain simplification. The mechanism that matters for a short-cycle automation company is that a downturn shows up in orders within a quarter or two and in sales a quarter after that; the orders growth reported this quarter is the cushion, and it is also the number that would fall first.

body: **BUY, target range $215–$255.** Honeywell Technologies opened its life as a pure-play automation company with sales up 4% organically, segment margin up 100 basis points, adjusted EPS up 10% to $1.95, orders far ahead of sales, and its growth, margin and earnings guidance raised; the forward multiple, as the valuation section argues, is fair for a business guided to double-digit earnings growth. The trailing figures on this page describe a company that no longer exists, and we have set them aside.

What we are paying for is the installed base and the margin bridge the moat section describes, toward the three-year earnings target management has set. What we cannot see is what moved the shares after July 2, 2026, what the standalone balance sheet and dividend look like, and whether the process business inflects on shipments rather than orders; those are the three gaps the thesis names, and they hold the target range below the Street's consensus.

We would raise the target on a third-quarter filing that shows a standalone balance sheet consistent with the free cash flow guidance and a process segment growing high single digits, and we would move to HOLD on a cut to the 2026 organic growth or segment margin guidance, on a disclosed cause for the decline that the fundamentals do not absorb, or on a rebased payout below what the market has assumed.
